column1: # Optional review records for cohesive files that benefit from explicit context.
# reviewed_lines is the factual size at review time, not a future limit.

column4: note

The builder is one order-sensitive decode walk. Symbol declarations, selection catalogs, operand encoding, first-level decode routing, and execution lifecycle now have separate owners without reordering emitted words.

Keep the memory-selection family cohesive: it is an ordinary translation unit, while the shared declaration and operand contracts are separate and the emitted gadget sequence remains reviewable as one family.

Keep the scalar-selection family cohesive: it is an ordinary translation unit, while the shared declaration and operand contracts are separate and the emitted gadget sequence remains reviewable as one family.

Keep the vector-selection family cohesive: it is an ordinary translation unit, while the shared declaration and operand contracts are separate and the emitted gadget sequence remains reviewable as one family.
Keep the generated precompiled-gadget ABI declaration catalog contiguous so declaration families remain mechanically comparable with the assembly banks.
Keep this assembly bank intact while its macro-local labels, symbol ordering, relocations, and measured hot-path layout remain coupled.
Keep complete system and atomic banks together while extraction would cross macro-local-label groups or change exported symbol and section layout.
Keep complete integer banks together while extraction would disturb exported-symbol ordering or measured section layout.
Keep complete load/store banks together while extraction would disturb exported-symbol ordering or measured section layout.
Keep the family-to-emitter bridge together because its register-residency and linked-exit rules form one compiler-family contract.

Keep the order-sensitive top-level lowering coordinator intact after family emitters, code emission, cache ownership, publication, linking, and executor lifecycle were separated. Split it further only when focused behavior and performance checks preserve the lowering contract.
Keep test-only compilation and publication-gate adapters separate from the production runtime API.
Retain one software-MMU generation and exception-atomic mutation owner. Native shadow lifetime is separately domain-owned.

Retain one connection-state and queue-transaction owner: wire framing, negotiated features, display, renderer, and GPU command semantics are already separate modules, while the remaining handlers mutate one negotiated protocol state and share one reset boundary.

Retain the guest-command state machine, including display metadata responses, as one exception-atomic protocol owner while renderer, display, and transport lifetimes remain separate, splitting only when a command family gains independently owned state or invariants.

Keep AppKit window, main-thread event, and native input ownership cohesive while common newest-frame-wins Metal presentation and reusable CPU framebuffer conversion remain separately owned device contracts.
Keep the software oracle next to its test support while that makes the specification mapping easier to audit, moving it only if a distinct reusable responsibility emerges.
Keep the family registrations together while the file remains a declarative index, extracting repeated registration mechanics when doing so improves navigation.
Keep engine orchestration and its mapping fixtures together while they share one harness contract, separating them if either becomes independently reusable.
Keep engine test registrations together as a declarative index, extracting repeated mechanics when doing so improves navigation.

Keep one owner for SIMD pair transfers: the allocated matrix, tagged-address matrix, and the compiled cubic program regression share the same variant table, expected-state helpers, and memory layout, and splitting them would duplicate that setup without separating any contract.
